title: Clean form fields with strip and isBlank

blocks.text: Java 11 added `isBlank()`, `strip()`, `stripLeading()` and `stripTrailing()` to `String`. The page's key distinction: `trim()` treats only characters up to `U+0020` as whitespace, while `strip()` uses `Character.isWhitespace`, so it also removes Unicode spaces such as EN QUAD (`U+2000`) and EM SPACE (`U+2003`). `isBlank()` is the modern form of `trim().isEmpty()`, with the same Unicode awareness.

Write `Fields.clean(List<String> raw)`. It returns the values of `raw`, in order, with **all surrounding whitespace removed, Unicode spaces included**, and leaves out every value that is **blank**: empty, or made only of whitespace of any kind.

cases.says: Each value comes back without surrounding whitespace, and blank values are dropped.
Unicode spaces such as EN QUAD (U+2000) around a value are removed too.
A value made only of Unicode spaces such as EM SPACE (U+2003) counts as blank and is dropped.

concepts: isBlank() is true for an empty string or one made only of whitespace, Unicode whitespace included.
strip() removes Unicode whitespace such as U+2000, which trim() leaves because it only knows characters up to U+0020.
